courses.title: Supply Chain and Operations Management
courses.description: Focuses on the integrative management of business activities intrinsic to the smooth flow of goods or services, information, and financial transactions across firms from raw materials to the end customer. This collaborative approach creates competitive advantages for all members of a supply chain. Emphasizes the responsibilities of managers regarding decisions concerning the design, operation, and control of supply chains and operations. Considers customers, globalization, corporate strategy, resources, sustainability, ethics, and diversity. Topics covered include customer-centric management; supply chain and operations strategies; process structure and control; and supply, inventory, and quality management. Emphasizes the key role of information technology, logistics network design, supply chain relationships, and process evolution.

courses.title: Global Supply Chain Strategy
courses.description: Focuses on the managerial activities of those involved in supply chain management operations and planning for companies doing international commerce. Analyzes contemporary issues that affect the design of international supply chain systems, including sourcing, logistics, transactions, risk, sustainability, and ethical considerations. Examines the current status and future prospects of the modes of international transportation as well as international trade and development issues, not only from the corporate perspective but also in terms of government policy.

courses.title: Supply Chain Management for Engineers
courses.description: Focuses on the qualitative frameworks, processes, and activities involved in the planning, transformation, and delivery of goods and services in a context uniquely geared to engineering students, who likely have already studied many of the key quantitative aspects of modern supply chain management. Offers students an opportunity to obtain foundational knowledge in key areas such as project management, supplier selection, legal aspects of supply chain management, supplier relational management, global sourcing, and logistics.

courses.title: Supply Chain Risk Management
courses.description: Explores the critical realm of mitigating supply chain disruptions within the dynamic landscape of contemporary business. Examines the intricacies of global supply chains, emphasizing real-world scenarios and exploring proactive measures such as diversification, technology integration, and strategic partnerships. Discusses challenges ranging from geopolitical uncertainties to natural disasters. Analyzes risk identification, assessment, and response strategies. Offers students an opportunity to gain practical insights into crisis communication, scenario planning, and the implementation of robust risk mitigation frameworks.

courses.title: Sourcing, Procurement, and Negotiation
courses.description: Addresses the strategic and operational role of sourcing and procurement and its impact on the supply chain as it relates to the entire organization. The selection, contracting, development and monitoring/managing of the right supplier in the right location is more often a source of competitive advantage and a major contributor to a company’s bottom line. The course focuses on a variety of aspects of this function—strategy development, organization, procedures, supplier selection, negotiations, buyer-supplier relationship management, quantity, quality, timeliness, and cost/price considerations for the purchase of goods and services.

courses.title: Supply Chain Analytics and Emerging Technologies
courses.description: Examines state-of-the-art in analytics capabilities and how they drive supply chains, from marketing to sourcing. Examines how organizations use analytics to meet their strategic objectives, provide value to the business, and make decisions. Offers students an opportunity to develop strategic supply chain decision-making skills using the latest analytics capabilities as an enabler. Focuses heavily on industry best practices, including looking at some of the leading companies.

courses.title: Logistics and Transportation Management
courses.description: Examines the logistics and transportation operations, including the structure, challenges, and potential of the major modes of domestic transportation. Focuses on the interaction between logistics providers and shippers in the marketplace. Explores the major dynamics of the logistics marketplace and their impact on supply chain management. Seeks to provide students with a managerial perspective on controlling what is typically the most expensive component of supply chain management, transportation expenditures.

courses.title: Managing Healthcare Operations and Supply Chain
courses.description: Focuses on concepts and topics related to the design and management of healthcare sector operations and supply chain. Offers students an opportunity to learn about practices and strategies for effective management of operations and supply chain in healthcare organizations, including management of inventory, operations processes, capacity, procurement, logistics, IT systems, and attendant relationships, as well as various optimization tools and techniques.

courses.title: Sustainable Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Focuses on how to create sustainable supply chains that profitably yield high-quality, safe products without supply interruption while creating a net benefit for the employees, community, and the environment. Studies how companies measure environmental performance and use the data to motivate associates, suppliers, customers, policymakers, and the public. Also addresses the impacts of global sustainability frameworks and measures.

courses.title: Junior/Senior Honors Project 1
courses.description: Focuses on in-depth project in which a student conducts research or produces a product related to the student’s major field. Combined with Junior/Senior Project 2 or college-defined equivalent for 8 credit honors project. May be repeated without limit.

courses.title: Special Topics in Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Offers special topics in Supply Chain Management. May be repeated once.

courses.title: Directed Study
courses.description: Offers independent work under the direction of faculty members of the department on a chosen topic. Course content depends on instructor. May be repeated up to four times for a maximum of 8 semester hours.

courses.title: Logistics and Transportation Management
courses.description: Examines the structure, operations, problems, and potential of the several major modes of transportation and focuses on the interaction between transportation service providers and shippers in the marketplace. Emphasizes the cost and service implications of transportation decisions within a broader logistics and supply chain management context. Presents a managerial perspective on controlling what is typically the most expensive component of supply chain management: transportation expenditure.

courses.title: Global Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Focuses on the managerial activities of those involved in supply chain management operations and planning for companies involved in international commerce. Analyzes contemporary issues that affect the design of international supply chain systems and strategies, including sourcing, logistics, and transactions. Examines the current status and future prospects of the modes of international logistics operations as well as international trade and development issues.

courses.title: Sourcing, Procurement, and Negotiations
courses.description: Explores the evolving landscape of strategic sourcing and advanced supplier management processes. Emphasizes cutting-edge technologies, sustainable practices, and ethical considerations. Examines modern strategic sourcing, blending theoretical and conceptual grounding with practical applications. Presents how to integrate sustainability into sourcing practices, focusing on minimizing environmental impact and promoting ethical supply chains. Analyzes supplier management processes including negotiation, contract management, relationship management, innovation sourcing, supplier development, supply risk management, corporate social responsibility, and international supplier considerations. Integrates both theoretical frameworks and practical applications to offer students an opportunity to obtain a deep understanding of how to effectively develop a sourcing strategy and manage suppliers in a dynamic environment.

courses.title: Analytics in Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Explores the state-of-the-art in analytics and quantitative capabilities and their impact on supply chains – from planning to returning. Designed to develop strategic decision-making skills using the latest analytical tools and techniques in an end-to-end supply chain, from sourcing and supply to logistics and transportation. Provides insights into how leading companies leverage advanced analytics to create value, improve resilience, and maintain a sustainable competitive advantage. Prepares students to apply analytical methods and enablers in real-world supply chain scenarios. Offers topics in retrospective and prospective analytics in supply chain processes. Examines best practices and case studies across various industries to illustrate the application of analytics in supply chain management.

courses.title: AI and Technology in Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Examines current technology and analytics capabilities and how they drive supply chains, from marketing to sourcing. Focuses on disruptive and transformational technology in an end-to-end supply chain such as blockchains, 3D printing, autonomous vehicles, digital twins, etc. Studies generative AI, including how it is used and/or should be used. Examines how leading organizations employ these technologies to meet strategic objectives, provide value to the business, and make decisions across supply chains.

courses.title: Managing Operations and the Supply Chain
courses.description: Focuses on the integrative management of processes and activities involved in transformation and delivery of goods and services. Emphasizes foundational knowledge on supply chain and operations management concepts, techniques, and functions. Covers sourcing and procurement, manufacturing and service operations, logistics management, process design and control, inventory management, interfirm relationship management, and attendant information flows.

courses.title: Risk Management and Business Continuity Planning
courses.description: Explores the area of risk management to offer students an opportunity to obtain tools to establish organizational agility and resilience. Emphasizes assessing threats in the supply chain, evaluating control alternatives, and strategy implementation approaches. Examines practical solutions that enable organizations to mitigate risk, manage a crisis, and recover after a disaster. Exposes students to different aspects of risk management with the goal of determining the most appropriate strategies and tactics to establish agile resiliency.

courses.title: Managing Healthcare Supply Chain Operations
courses.description: Introduces various tools and techniques and examines concepts and topics that enhance the design and effective management of operations and supply chains in healthcare organizations. Focuses on activities and functions such as managing operations processes, demand and capacity planning, inventory management, logistics, procurement, relationship management, information technology systems and innovations, and emerging trends.

courses.title: Directed Study
courses.description: Offers independent work under the direction of members of the department on chosen topics. May be repeated without limit.
